transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump says he agrees with Vice President Vance, who wrote earlier today that cost
increases as a result of Trump's decision to strike Iran were one of the big reasons
behind Republican midterm election losses.
But as NPR's Emily Fang reports, Trump also said he did not regret his decision to start
the war.
Trump talked to Vance before the Vice President published a long post on social media site
X blaming the Iran war for the Democrats taking control of Congress.
"Probably it's true, but at the same time if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it
again, because long term, it's the only answer.
You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon."
Then Trump celebrated the last steel ceiling beam being placed in his east wing ballroom
construction site as hundreds of construction workers cheered and extolled the quality of
marble in construction used in the ballroom.
Emily Fang, NPR News, The White House.
Mid-term voters weighed in on ballot measures across the country on topics ranging from
abortion to taxes to guns, NPR's Rachel Treisman reports.
Voters in 39 states, D.C. and the Northern Mariana Islands considered a total of 146 statewide
ballot initiatives this midterm season.
Several states moved to protect LGBTQ rights, including Virginia, which removed its constitutional
ban on same-sex marriage.
Voters like Colorado and Arizona restricted transgender students' access to school sports.
Taxes were on the ballot, too.
Floridians voted to cut property taxes for homeowners.
Tennessee voters prohibited their government from collecting a statewide property tax,
while Arizona voters limited new taxes on groceries.
Three states voted to protect access to abortion.
Massachusetts voted in support of gun control legislation, while Idaho residents voted to
choose an official state gun.
Rachel Treisman, NPR News.
The Dow surged today, closing up more than 1,500 points, or more than 3 percent, and
PR's Rafael Naum reports.
There were two main reasons.
First, we did not get a contested election, which many investors had feared would lead
to volatility.
Instead, President Trump said he would accept the results.
Secondly, investors also tend to prefer divided government, because they think it can prevent
potential accesses.
But it's not clear if the stock market gains would be sustained.
Democrats could pursue stronger regulations against businesses, especially when it comes
to AI and data centers.
And Elon Musk's companies, Tesla and SpaceX, tumbled after the billionaires spent hundreds
of millions of dollars trying to elect more Republicans.
Rafael Naum, NPR News.
Russian attacks on critical infrastructure have caused power and water outages in key
chief and surrounding areas that lasted hours.
Rescuers are still searching for survivors in southern Ukraine after a deadly attack
there.
Officials from the U.S., Germany, France, Britain, NATO, and the EU are meeting in Brussels
to discuss a post-war support for Ukraine.
This is NPR.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog began consultations on forming a new government after last week's
elections there.
Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party, nor that of his main challenger, former
military chief Gadi Eizencote, secured an outright majority in parliament.
Both sides are now locked in negotiations to persuade smaller parties to join a governing
coalition.
Conductor Herbert Blumstedt has died at age 99, with a career spanning more than seven
decades.
He was perhaps the oldest working conductor in history, and Pierre's Tom Heisinger reports.
Herbert Blumstedt led most of the world's best orchestras, including a 10-year stint
directing the San Francisco Symphony.
Joshua Kossman, former classical music critic for the San Francisco Chronicle, says Blumstedt
inherited an orchestra that was skilled but lacking in discipline.
Under his guidance, everything became sharper, cleaner, more crisply focused.
Blumstedt was born in 1927 in Springfield, Massachusetts, to Swedish parents.
John Cage and Leonard Bernstein were among his teachers.
His conducting debut came in 1954.
"Retirement is not a question of age," he once said.
"I love music so much, I can't give up."
And he didn't.
Tom Heisinger, NPR News.
The NFL's Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons face off in Madrid, Spain this Sunday.
The game will be played at legendary football club Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu Stadium.
It will be the second NFL regular season game in the Spanish capital after the Miami Dolphins
beat the Washington commanders last year.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Trump says he agrees with Vance that Iran war costs hurt Republicans, but would strike again
Trump celebrates final steel beam placement at White House east wing ballroom construction
Voters in 39 states weigh in on 146 statewide ballot measures, including abortion, taxes, guns
Virginia removes constitutional ban on same-sex marriage in midterm ballot vote
Florida voters approve property tax cuts for homeowners; Tennessee bans statewide property tax
Dow surges more than 1,500 points after midterms avoid contested election
Russian attacks cause hours-long power and water outages in Ukraine; rescuers search for survivors
Israeli President Herzog begins coalition consultations after inconclusive elections, Netanyahu and Eizencote
Conductor Herbert Blumstedt dies at 99 after career spanning more than seven decades
NFL's Bengals and Falcons to play regular season game at Real Madrid's Bernabeu Stadium Sunday
